new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (language not in catalog, no existing statements). This is transcription evidence only, not a source statement; it is consistent with the earlier script tabulation of Taber's (1993) 193-item Tela list (141/193 penult, 31 final = mostly prefix + closed monosyllabic root, 11 antepenult with post-tonic iV) and with the two stress-marked notes in the typed companion ([ɛˈɛrɛ], [nbɔˈtɔk]). A prose statement on Tela stress still does not exist in any source read; the unreleased/other-bundle candidates (Emplawas Grammar Sketch, EMW-Sketch, access U; a different language) would not supply one for Tela.
new_statements.rule_in_words: DATA OBSERVATION, not an author's statement: where Edwards marks primary stress on a Tela form, the mark sits on the penultimate syllable of the phonetic word in vowel-final forms (the root syllable before the nominal suffix -ɛ/-e: ˈwakyɛ, ˈkanɛ, ˈrɛmɛ, pɔˈpɔrɛ, muˈnimɛ, ɛrˈpayɛ, ˈpanːɛ) and on the final syllable of a number of consonant-final forms (ɔˈpak 'woman', unˈβak 'girl', nɛˈnɛn 'bleat/shout', nbɔˈtɔk 'stupid', ˈamir excepted), i.e. surface stress predominantly penultimate, with final stress where the form ends in a closed root syllable (compare Taber 1993 opˈpaki 'woman' with final -i vs Edwards ɔˈpak). Many items, especially in the later verb/adjective pages, carry no stress mark at all. The scan states no rule, nothing on secondary stress, weight or predictability.
new_statements.exceptions: none stated (source is a wordlist); observed final-stress forms are consonant-final (ɔˈpak, unˈβak, nɛˈnɛn, nbɔˈtɔk, tyɛnˈɛ? 'why' uncertain reading); a few forms with a final iɛ/yɛ/ɪɛ sequence look antepenultimate if the sequence is disyllabic (ˈɔtyɛ 'person', ˈniβrɪɛ 'wing'), matching Taber's ˈotije class
new_statements.identity_note: Tela variety of Tela-Masbuar as spoken in Desa Tela, Kecamatan Babar Barat (west Babar Island), four male speakers aged 57-68 all born in Tela; no Masbuar data in the scan.
